title: ByteDance's Doubao launches utility bill payments in China, accelerating conversational service expansion
source_used: BigGo Finance (relaying Dujia and Wall Street CN)
key_facts: ByteDance's AI assistant Doubao has launched water, electricity and gas bill payment, started by voice or text command.
People close to Doubao confirmed this to Dujia on 9 October; Wall Street CN and Dujia tested it.
Users must log in with a Douyin account and bind their utility account numbers; the assistant shows a service card that redirects to a payment page.
Availability varies by city and category; some regions show all three services as "not yet available".
The chat only triggers the process; binding, confirming and paying still happen on the linked page, with payments provided by Douyin Pay and other third parties.
On 30 September Doubao added flight, train, ride-hailing and navigation services ("Travel with Doubao"), with partners including Caocao Mobility and Baidu Maps.
Alibaba's Tongyi Qianwen already offers a more complete conversational service loop, including in-chat payment in many scenarios; Doubao still lacks food delivery.
quote_evidence: ByteDance's AI assistant Doubao has officially launched utility bill payment features, allowing users to directly initiate water, electricity, and gas payments through voice or text commands.
People close to Doubao confirmed to Dujia on October 9 that the assistant is progressively building out service capabilities across life scenarios including travel and utility payments.
To be clear, conversational activation only handles the trigger step.
why_it_matters_hint: Chinese users get a chat route to routine bills, but coverage is patchy and the payment steps stay outside the chat.
notes: BigGo Finance is an aggregator relaying Chinese reporting (Dujia, Wall Street CN); it adds its own analysis. First reporter taken as Dujia.
